title: Downstream preview cascade mixes submodel edges with parent-graph nodes, so the cascade is silently dead when a node inside an opened submodel changes columns
description: Inside fetchPreviewImmediate the cascade builds its adjacency from graphRef.current.edges but resolves its node set from resolveGraphFromRefs(...).nodes. When a submodel is drilled in, graphRef.current holds the SUBMODEL canvas (nodes+edges) while parentGraphRef.current is set, so resolveGraphFromRefs returns the PARENT graph's nodes. propagate therefore walks submodel edge IDs to compute reachableNodeIds, but drainReadyQueue looks those submodel child IDs up in cascadeNodes (= parent nodes) via cascadeNodes.find(n => n.id === nodeId). The lookup misses every time, so each downstream child hits the `if (!dsNode || !canPreviewNode(dsNode)) { settleNode(nodeId, false); continue }` branch and the cascade no-ops: downstream nodes inside a submodel never get re-previewed (their _columns / requestedPreviewColumns are not refreshed) after an upstream column change. At the top level parentGraphRef.current is null so resolveGraphFromRefs returns graphRef.current.edges/nodes and the two sources coincide — the defect is submodel-specific.
evidence: Line 318 `const graph = resolveGraphFromRefs(graphRef, parentGraphRef, submodelsRef, preambleRef)` then line 319 `let cascadeNodes = graph.nodes`; resolveGraphFromRefs (buildGraph.ts:31-33) returns parentGraphRef.current.nodes/edges when parentGraphRef.current != null. propagate line 332 `const { edges } = graphRef.current` builds childrenBySource from the SUBMODEL edges; BFS at 346-353 yields submodel node IDs in reachableNodeIds. drainReadyQueue line 439 `const dsNode = cascadeNodes.find((n) => n.id === nodeId)` searches PARENT nodes → undefined → line 440-442 `if (!dsNode || !canPreviewNode(dsNode)) { settleNode(nodeId, false); continue }`. useSubmodelNavigation.handleDrillIntoSubmodel sets parentGraphRef.current to the parent while setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw load the submodel into graphRef; useEdgeHandlers.onNodeClick (useEdgeHandlers.ts:351) calls fetchPreview unconditionally for nodes inside the submodel, so the path is reachable.
